generatedProse.concept-context: Across disciplines, a reference is not written freehand; it is built from a fixed set of elements placed in a set order. A book, for example, adds the title, the edition, the place of publication and the publisher to the author and year. Once you know the pattern for each kind of source, you can build an accurate reference without guessing, and check it against the pattern before it goes in your list.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two students reference the same book in their work.

Student A copies the reference straight from the library catalogue: SMITH, Alex. A Short Guide To Study. 2021. Published by Field Press. The elements are mostly there, but the order and formatting are wrong. The first name is spelled out, the title is over-capitalised, the year sits in the wrong place, and the edition and place of publication are missing. This is what copying from a database often produces.

Student B builds the reference by hand from the pattern: Smith, A. (2021) A short guide to study. 2nd edn. London: Field Press. Surname then initial, year in brackets, title, edition, then place of publication and publisher. It is accurate, consistent, and ready for an alphabetical list.

Both students had the same book. Only Student B's reference would pass a marker's eye.
generatedProse.summary: A reference is built from a fixed set of elements in a set order, and each kind of source has its own pattern. Build each reference yourself from that pattern, rather than trusting a database to do it for you, and check it before it goes in your list. You can now assemble an accurate reference element by element. The next lesson is about the style that sets these patterns, and applying it consistently.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Student B's reference accurate where Student A's was not?

items.text: It followed the fixed order and formatting, built by hand from the pattern element by element.
It was copied more carefully from the same database.
It used more of the author's full name and more capital letters.
It left out some elements to keep the entry short.

feedback.correct: That's right. Building from the pattern kept every element in the right place.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Compare how each reference handled the order and formatting of the elements.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B's reference was accurate because it followed the fixed order and formatting, built by hand rather than copied from the database.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
